pages.text:
Dorian Lynskey follows the making and afterlife of George Orwell’s Nineteen Eighty-Four. He connects the novel with Orwell’s experiences, political arguments and literary influences before tracing the different uses readers have made of it since publication.

This is a history of a book and its cultural reach, rather than another fictional visit to Oceania. It examines how Orwell’s language and imagined institutions entered public debate, and why changing generations continue to find their own anxieties reflected in them.
